name: éric

attributes.attribute: paid on murder, rape, or slander
records that éric led to further bloodshed

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Éric is the Irish legal concept of honor-price. The word also appears as eric, éraic, dire-fine, and lóg n-enech. It sets a value on every person by social rank. Celtic Ireland had no police force and no court of law. Each person therefore carried a fixed honor-price. The killer or injurer paid this price on murder or harm to the victim's kin group. A person of higher rank who harmed a lower-rank person paid the value in gold, cattle, slaves, or other goods. The law also demanded éric for rape and slander. Because the whole kinship group had to pay a debt, the law curbed young, violent men. The honor-price is a central theme of Irish myth. In the tale of the Sons of Tuireann, the brothers killed Cian. To pay the price, they had to perform impossible feats. The Senchas Mór, a collection of Irish legal texts, records that a demand for éric often led to further bloodshed.

okr.objective: éric is the Irish legal concept of honor-price.
